plants.name: Dimorphotheca sinuata
plants.description: Glowing orange daisies with dark centers carpet the veld in sheets of color. The flowers follow the sun, opening wide on bright mornings and closing on cloudy days.
plants.bloomingSeason: August to September, with the strongest displays from mid-August to mid-October, depending on winter rains
plants.location: Namaqualand and the West Coast of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Namaqualand daisies are heliotropic. Their petals close at night and in cloudy weather, so a fully open field depends on warm sunshine.

plants.name: Lespedeza thunbergii
plants.description: Long, arching branches spill over with tiny magenta-purple pea-shaped blossoms. In late summer the shrub looks like a fountain of color.
plants.location: Japan, where it is grown in temple gardens and along countryside paths
plants.funFact: Hagi is one of the seven flowers of autumn in Japanese tradition and has long been celebrated in poetry. It also fixes nitrogen, which enriches the soil around it.

plants.name: Solidago lepida
plants.description: Soft golden plumes rise above the meadows and roadsides in late summer. They hum with bees, butterflies and other pollinators stocking up before autumn.
plants.location: Rocky Mountain region of western North America
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and is carried by insects. The usual culprit is ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Acacia drummondii
plants.description: This rounded shrub has feathery, fern-like leaves. In late winter and spring it is topped with bright golden flower spikes.
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, the first day of spring. Gardeners often choose wattles like this one so that something is in flower on that date.
